title: Not All Layers Are Equal in Image-to-Video Transfer
summary: Across four video-native model families and two pretraining paradigms, the study found that temporal sensitivity changes with transformer depth and differs between vision-only and vision-language models. Its STRAP layer-placement rule improved accuracy by up to 11.8% across four fine-grained action-recognition benchmarks, with fewer trainable parameters; these are benchmark results.
organization: University of Stuttgart; University of Hildesheim; University Hospital Heidelberg; University of Münster

evidence.tested: Across four video-native model families and two pretraining paradigms, the study found that temporal sensitivity changes with transformer depth and differs between vision-only and vision-language models. evidence.unknown: The study evaluates the reported models and datasets only; broader generalization and real-world deployment outcomes were not established.
evidence.ai_role: Layer-wise temporal-sensitivity analysis of video foundation models motivated STRAP, a training-free rule that assigns spatial and temporal adapters to different layer ranges.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
